Use 2-space indentation, double quotes, trailing commas, and semicolons matching the repository Prettier and ESLint configuration.
Order imports with external/workspace packages (`@excalidraw/common`, `@excalidraw/math`, `@excalidraw/element`) first, followed by relative imports and `import type` declarations.
Keep all functions in `packages/element/src/textStyleRanges.ts` pure and side-effect-free: never mutate input range arrays or range objects in place.
Write tests using Vitest (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi`) and `@testing-library/react` helpers (`render`, `fireEvent`, `act`, `API`, `UI`, `Keyboard`, `Pointer`).

decisions.choice: Store `TextStyleRange` entries as `{ readonly start: number; readonly end: number; readonly strokeColor?: string; readonly backgroundColor?: string }` in 0-based end-exclusive UTF-16 code-unit offsets into `element.originalText`, and set `textStyleRanges` as a standard enumerable own property (`normalizeTextStyleRanges(...)`, defaulting to `[]`) on `ExcalidrawTextElement` in `newTextElement`, `restoreElement`, `deepCopyElement`, `ElementsDelta.applyDelta`, and clipboard serialize/parse.
rejected: Defining a non-enumerable hidden accessor via `Object.defineProperty` on text elements
decisions.reason: `originalText` offsets survive line wrapping and reflow, and a standard enumerable own `textStyleRanges` array (defaulting to `[]`) is preserved across all object spreads (`newElementWith` / `mutateElement`), JSON serialisation, clipboard copy/paste, restore, duplication, and history deltas.

decisions.topic: Canonical range normalisation and overlap resolution
decisions.choice: Use elementary interval decomposition over all range boundary points in `normalizeTextStyleRanges` and `applyTextStyleRange` so later ranges override earlier ranges per property (`strokeColor` vs `backgroundColor` independently), drop ranges with `start >= end` or neither style set, drop `backgroundColor: "transparent"` and `strokeColor === elementStrokeColor`, sort by `start`, and merge adjacent intervals with identical `strokeColor` and `backgroundColor`.
rejected: Allowing overlapping ranges at render time
Replacing the entire style object when only one of `strokeColor` or `backgroundColor` is applied
decisions.reason: Elementary interval decomposition guarantees deterministic, non-overlapping canonical ranges while preserving orthogonal inline styles (`strokeColor` when applying `backgroundColor`, and vice versa).

decisions.topic: WYSIWYG inline selection tracking vs initial mount auto-select
decisions.choice: Track the active textarea selection in `packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.tsx` and expose `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(element?)`, treating the initial mount `editable.select()` (when `autoSelect && !pendingInitialSelection`) as non-inline until the selection is set via `initialSelection` or changed after mount via `setSelectionRange`, `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` setters, or user selection events, and preserving the last active selection when clicking properties UI.
rejected: Treating `editable.selectionStart < editable.selectionEnd` on initial mount as an active inline range selection
Reading `document.activeElement` only at action execution time without preserving selection across properties UI pointerdown
decisions.reason: On editor open, `editable.select()` selects all text by default; excluding the untouched initial auto-select preserves existing element-wide and sticky-note colour picker behaviour when no explicit substring selection has been made.

decisions.topic: Inline highlight colour picker availability during text editing
decisions.choice: Render `app.actionManager.renderAction("changeBackgroundColor")` inside `actionChangeStrokeColor.PanelComponent` when `appState.editingTextElement` is active and not bound to a sticky note (since sticky-note labels already render `changeBackgroundColor`), and resolve `resolveColorTarget` for `backgroundColor` to the `regular` domain (including `"transparent"`) when `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection` is active.
rejected: Modifying `getShapeActionPredicates` in `shapeActionPredicates.ts` to enable `backgroundColor` for all text elements
Creating a separate action registration for text highlight colour
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert `getShapeActionPredicates(...).backgroundColor === false` for plain text elements and `shapeActionPredicates.ts` is outside the write allowlist; rendering `changeBackgroundColor` inside `actionChangeStrokeColor.PanelComponent` when editing non-sticky text exposes inline highlight controls and allows `"transparent"` to clear highlights.

units.behaviour: Provide pure functions for normalising, applying, shifting, comparing, and mapping `TextStyleRange` entries onto wrapped text lines and visual runs.
rules: 1. Export `type TextStyleRun = { readonly text: string; readonly start: number; readonly end: number; readonly strokeColor?: string; readonly backgroundColor?: string }` and re-export `type { TextStyleRange }` from `./types`.

2. `normalizeTextStyleRanges(ranges, textLength, elementStrokeColor?)`: return `[]` if `!Array.isArray(ranges) || ranges.length === 0 || !Number.isFinite(textLength) || textLength <= 0`; clamp integer `start` and `end` to `[0, Math.floor(textLength)]`; drop entries with `start >= end`; treat `strokeColor` as undefined if empty, `"transparent"`, or equal to `elementStrokeColor`; treat `backgroundColor` as undefined if empty or `"transparent"`; resolve overlaps using sorted elementary intervals `[points[i], points[i + 1])` where later input ranges override earlier ranges per property (`strokeColor` and `backgroundColor` independently while preserving non-overridden properties); sort by ascending `start` and merge adjacent intervals (`prev.end === next.start`) when both `strokeColor` and `backgroundColor` match.

3. `applyTextStyleRange(ranges, textLength, selection, style, elementStrokeColor?)`: normalise `ranges` first; if `!selection || !Number.isFinite(selection.start) || !Number.isFinite(selection.end)` or clamped `selStart >= selEnd`, return normalised ranges; otherwise decompose over elementary intervals including `selStart` and `selEnd`, applying `style.strokeColor` (clearing when empty, `"transparent"`, or equal to `elementStrokeColor`) and/or `style.backgroundColor` (clearing when empty or `"transparent"`) across `[selStart, selEnd)` while preserving orthogonal properties on overlapping sub-intervals, omitting intervals with neither property left, and merging adjacent identical intervals.

4. `shiftTextStyleRangesOnEdit(ranges, prevText, nextText)`: normalise `ranges` against `prevText.length`; if `prevText === nextText` return normalised ranges; if `normalized.length === 0 || nextText.length === 0` return `[]`; compute minimal edit splice via common prefix `changeStart` and common suffix (`changeEnd` in `prevText`, `insertedLength`, `delta = insertedLength - (changeEnd - changeStart)`); keep ranges with `end <= changeStart` unchanged, shift ranges with `start >= changeEnd` by `delta`, drop ranges with `changeEnd > changeStart && start >= changeStart && end <= changeEnd`, and for partially overlapping/spanning ranges set `newStart = start < changeStart ? start : start === changeStart && end > changeEnd && insertedLength > 0 ? changeStart : changeStart + insertedLength` and `newEnd = end > changeEnd ? end + delta : changeStart`, then pass through `normalizeTextStyleRanges(..., nextText.length)`.

5. `getWrappedLineTextRuns(line, ranges)`: slice `WrappedTextLine` (`{ text, start, end }`) into contiguous `TextStyleRun[]` covering `[line.start, line.end)` using `line.text.slice(runStart - line.start, runEnd - line.start)`; return a single unstyled run `[{ text: line.text, start: line.start, end: line.end }]` when `line.end <= line.start` or no ranges intersect `[line.start, line.end)`.

6. `getWrappedTextLinesForElement(element, maxWidth?, env?)` and `getTextElementLineRuns(element, env?, maxWidth?)`: use `getWrappedTextLines` from `./textWrapping` with `getFontString(element)` (when `maxWidth` is omitted, use `Infinity` if `normalizedText === normalizedOriginalText`, else try `getWrappedTextLines(normalizedOriginalText, font, element.width, env)` and if its line texts differ from `element.text.replace(/
?/g, "
").split("
")`, align the split visual lines sequentially against `normalizedOriginalText` skipping soft-wrap whitespace or `
` between lines), then map each `WrappedTextLine` with `getWrappedLineTextRuns`.

7. `getSelectionTextStyle(element, selection)`: slice `[selection.start, selection.end)` with `getWrappedLineTextRuns` against normalised ranges and return `{ strokeColor: string | null; backgroundColor: string | null }` where `strokeColor` is the common `run.strokeColor ?? element.strokeColor` across all runs in the selection (`null` if mixed) and `backgroundColor` is the common `run.backgroundColor ?? "transparent"` across all runs in the selection (`null` if mixed).
8. `areTextStyleRangesEqual(a, b)`: return `true` when both range lists normalise/have equal length and identical `start`, `end`, `strokeColor`, and `backgroundColor` at every index.

2. In `drawElementOnCanvas` for `isTextElement(element)`, if `!element.textStyleRanges?.length`, execute the existing single `context.fillText(lines[index], horizontalOffset, index * lineHeightPx + verticalOffset)` loop unchanged (NFR-3).
3. If `element.textStyleRanges?.length` is non-zero, compute `const font = getFontString(element);` and `const lineRuns = getTextElementLineRuns(element, renderConfig.renderEnvironment);`.

4. For each visual line `index`, compute `lineText = lines[index] ?? ""`, `lineWidth = getLineWidth(lineText, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)`, and `lineStartX = element.textAlign === "center" ? (element.width - lineWidth) / 2 : element.textAlign === "right" ? element.width - lineWidth : 0`.

In Pass 1 (background highlights), for each run in `lineRuns[index]` with a non-empty, non-`"transparent"` `backgroundColor` and `run.text.length > 0`, compute `prefixWidth = getLineWidth(prefixText, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)` and `runWidth = getLineWidth(run.text, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)`, `runX = rtl ? lineStartX + (lineWidth - prefixWidth - runWidth) : lineStartX + prefixWidth`, set `context.fillStyle = applyDarkModeFilter(run.backgroundColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK)`, and call `context.fillRect(runX, index * lineHeightPx, runWidth, lineHeightPx)`.

6. In Pass 2 (glyph ink), set `context.textAlign = rtl ? "right" : "left"`, and for each run in `lineRuns[index]` with `run.text.length > 0`, set `context.fillStyle = applyDarkModeFilter(run.strokeColor ?? element.strokeColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK)` and call `context.fillText(run.text, rtl ? runX + runWidth : runX, index * lineHeightPx + verticalOffset)`.

In `actionChangeStrokeColor.perform`, if `appState.editingTextElement` is active, resolve `editingText = elementsMap.get(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement`; if `isTextElement(editingText)` and `const selection = getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText)` is non-null, compute `nextRanges = applyTextStyleRange(editingText.textStyleRanges, editingText.originalText.length, selection, { strokeColor: color }, editingText.strokeColor)`, update only `editingText` in `elements` with `newElementWith(el, { textStyleRanges: nextRanges }, true)`, and return `{ elements: nextElements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: nextEditingTextElement }, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }` without mutating element-level `strokeColor`, sticky-note ink, or `currentItem*` defaults.

3. In `actionChangeStrokeColor.PanelComponent`, resolve `editingText = appState.editingTextElement ? (app.scene.getElement<ExcalidrawTextElement>(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement) : null` and `selection = editingText && isTextElement(editingText) ? getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText) : null`; when `selection` is non-null, pass `getSelectionTextStyle(editingText, selection).strokeColor` as `color` to `ColorPicker`; also when `editingText && isTextElement(editingText) && !isStickyNoteBoundText(editingText, app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap())`, render `{app.actionManager.renderAction("changeBackgroundColor")}` after `ColorPicker` so inline highlight controls are available while editing any non-sticky text element.

4. In `actionChangeBackgroundColor.perform`, if `appState.editingTextElement` is active, resolve `editingText = elementsMap.get(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement`; if `isTextElement(editingText)` and `const selection = getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText)` is non-null, compute `nextRanges = applyTextStyleRange(editingText.textStyleRanges, editingText.originalText.length, selection, { backgroundColor: color }, editingText.strokeColor)`, update only `editingText` in `elements` with `newElementWith(el, { textStyleRanges: nextRanges }, true)`, and return `{ elements: nextElements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: nextEditingTextElement }, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }` without mutating container/sticky-note `backgroundColor` or `currentItem*` defaults.

5. In `actionChangeBackgroundColor.PanelComponent`, resolve `editingText = appState.editingTextElement ? (app.scene.getElement<ExcalidrawTextElement>(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement) : null` and `selection = editingText && isTextElement(editingText) ? getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText) : null`; when `selection` is non-null, pass `getSelectionTextStyle(editingText, selection).backgroundColor` as `color` to `ColorPicker`.

units.behaviour: Unit-test `normalizeTextStyleRanges`, `applyTextStyleRange`, `shiftTextStyleRangesOnEdit`, `getWrappedLineTextRuns`, `getTextElementLineRuns`, `getSelectionTextStyle`, `areTextStyleRangesEqual`, `newTextElement`, `newElementWith`, `deepCopyElement`, `duplicateElement`, `convertToExcalidrawElements`, and `ElementsDelta`.

units.behaviour: Integration-test WYSIWYG inline substring styling, live edit range shifting, reflow invariance, Canvas 2D run/highlight rendering, SVG `<rect>`/`<tspan>` export, clipboard copy/paste, undo/redo, duplication, and reconciliation.
rules: 1. Render `<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />` and test opening the WYSIWYG editor on a text element, selecting a substring `[start, end)` via `setSelectionRange`, and executing `actionChangeStrokeColor` and `actionChangeBackgroundColor` (as well as clicking top-pick swatches in the properties panel) to apply, split, merge, and clear (`"transparent"` and base `element.strokeColor`) inline ranges while verifying initial auto-select and collapsed caret apply element-wide / sticky-note colours (AC-1).

2. Test typing/editing in `.excalidraw-wysiwyg` (`updateTextEditor` / `fireEvent.input`) to verify `textStyleRanges` shift on insertion, deletion, and replacement before, inside, and across ranges on both the scene element and `h.state.editingTextElement` (AC-2).

3. Test changing font size (`actionChangeFontSize`), font family (`actionChangeFontFamily`), text alignment (`actionChangeTextAlign`), and bound container width to verify `textStyleRanges` are preserved and map onto newly wrapped lines (AC-3, FR-10).

4. Test `exportScene({ type: "canvas", ... })` and `exportScene({ type: "svg", ... })` in both light and dark themes (`THEME.DARK`) to verify Canvas `fillRect` highlights and per-run `fillText` calls, SVG `<rect>` highlight elements and `<tspan fill="...">` child elements, dark-mode `applyDarkModeFilter` inversion, and unchanged output for unstyled text elements (AC-4, AC-5, NFR-3, NFR-4).

5. Test clipboard copy/paste via `serializeAsClipboardJSON`, `createPasteEvent`, `parseClipboard`, and `h.app.pasteFromClipboard` on both styled and legacy unstyled text elements to verify `textStyleRanges` survives clipboard copy/paste with normalised, deep-cloned range arrays (FR-12, AC-6).
6. Test `Keyboard.undo()` / `Keyboard.redo()`, `duplicateElements`, `reconcileElements`, and `convertToExcalidrawElements` to verify `textStyleRanges` round-trip fidelity (AC-6, AC-7).
